newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen bullish, but pace of gains may slow.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen bullish, but pace of gains may slow.

text.p: The dollar is expected to stay strong against the yen and the mark in Asia on Thursday after fresh gains overnight, although the pace of rise of the dollar against the yen may slow down, dealers said.
"Sentiment is still strong," said a trust bank dealer. "But the pace of the dollar rise may slow down," he added.
U.S. fund operators are quick to take profits after purchases, while Japanese investors have failed to buy enough dollars at lower levels, he said.
Profit-taking is likely to kick in at around 127.20/30 yen, before dollar tests next resistance at 127.50 yen, he added.
The dollar closed stronger in New York on Wednesday after reaching a 37-month high against the mark and a more than four-and-a-half year peak at 127 yen.
Dealers said Wednesday's gains in Tokyo were mainly driven by purchases by securities houses and trust banks. Major life insurers have not been detected in the currency market.
"Expectations that major life insurers may enter the market around next week could support the bullish sentiment," said the trust bank dealer.
The dollar's downside is expected to be well-supported at around 126.50 yen, he added.
Easing fears of Bank of Japan (BOJ) dollar-selling intervention were also behind the dollar's rapid rise by more than two yen since the start of this week.
"I don't think that the BOJ will step in to stem the dollar's rise soon," said a city bank dealer.

"The 130 yen level may be the point at which the BOJ may do so," he added. He and other dealers said operators were holding on to some dollar long positions, but the amount was not so large. This leaves the question of whether dollar sales intervention can be carried out effectively.
